{{short description|Notion of boundary associated with a group}}
In [[mathematics]], specifically [[harmonic analysis]] and [[probability theory]], the '''Furstenberg boundary''' is a notion of [[boundary of a set|boundary]] associated with a [[group (mathematics)|group]].  It is named for [[Harry Furstenberg]], who introduced it in a series of papers beginning in 1963 (in the case of semisimple [[Lie group]]s).  The Furstenberg boundary can be characterized as a universal boundary space for harmonic analysis on the group, in the sense that bounded [[harmonic function]]s can be represented by their boundary values via a [[Poisson kernel|Poisson-type integral]].

For example, when <math>G=\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})</math>, the Furstenberg boundary is the real projective line <math>\mathbb{RP}^1</math>, which may be identified with the boundary circle of the hyperbolic plane, and the Poisson-like integral is the usual [[Poisson kernel]] for the [[upper half-plane]].

== Semisimple Lie groups ==

Let <math>G</math> be a connected [[semisimple Lie group]].  The Furstenberg boundary of <math>G</math> is the homogeneous space
:<math display="block">G/P,</math>
where <math>P</math> is a minimal [[Borel subgroup#Parabolic subgroups|parabolic subgroup]] of <math>G</math>.

This space is compact and homogeneous under the action of <math>G</math>.  More generally, quotients <math>G/Q</math> by parabolic subgroups <math>Q</math> are generalized flag manifolds, and the Furstenberg boundary is the maximal one among these in the sense that every quotient by a parabolic subgroup is a factor of <math>G/P</math>.

For example, if <math>G=\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb R)</math>, then the Furstenberg boundary is the manifold of complete flags in <math>\mathbb R^n</math>.  For <math>G=\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb R)</math>, it is <math>\mathbb{RP}^1</math>.

== Relation to Poisson boundaries ==

Let <math>\mu</math> be a probability measure on <math>G</math>.  A function <math>f</math> on <math>G</math> is called <math>\mu</math>-harmonic if
:<math display="block">f(g)=\int_G f(gg')\,d\mu(g').</math>

The [[Poisson boundary]] of the measured group <math>(G,\mu)</math> is a measure space that represents bounded <math>\mu</math>-harmonic functions by boundary integrals.  Unlike the Furstenberg boundary, the Poisson boundary depends on the choice of the measure <math>\mu</math>.

For semisimple Lie groups, Furstenberg showed that for broad classes of measures the Poisson boundary can be realized on a homogeneous boundary of the form <math>G/Q</math>, where <math>Q</math> is a parabolic subgroup.  In particular situations the maximal boundary <math>G/P</math> plays the role of a universal homogeneous boundary from which the others are obtained as quotients.
